item.title: Why Antigravity Eats Weekly Quota Fast - and What I Measured
item.author: asubedi@asubedi.com.np (Ashish Subedi)
item.description:
Gemini 4 Hydrogen, Gemini 4 Argon, and hy4-flash via OpenCode used for the binary reverse engineering, empirical cache probing, and keep-alive tooling.

Introduction

Greetings! If you use Google Antigravity (agy) with the big frontier models, you have probably noticed how fast your weekly quota disappears during normal coding sessions [1, 4].

My suspicion was simple: a short prompt-cache lifetime. When you are coding with an agent, you don’t send messages every 10 seconds. You wait for a response, read the diff, run a test, think for 5 minutes, and then send your next prompt. If the prompt cache expires during that 5-minute pause, your next message has to re-ingest the entire conversation history at full price.

item.title: Speculative Decoding
item.author: asubedi@asubedi.com.np (Ashish Subedi)
item.description:
This is part 2 of the LLM inference series. Part 1: I Kinda Understand LLM Serving.

Introduction

Greetings! In the last post, I went through continuous batching and PagedAttention. This time we are looking at Speculative Decoding, a technique that speeds up LLM generation without any loss in output quality.

The idea: use a small, fast model to guess what the big model would say, then verify all those guesses in one shot. If the guesses are correct, you got free tokens. If some are wrong, you fix them and move on. The output is mathematically identical to just running the big model directly. No quality loss. Just speed.

item.title: I Kinda Understand LLM Serving
item.author: asubedi@asubedi.com.np (Ashish Subedi)
item.description:
LLM is used in every stage of this blog (learning, coding, and writing of this blog).

Introduction

Greetings! Welcome aboard to my humble blog. Recently, I have been trying to understand the internals of LLM serving. “Why?” you ask? Okay, let me rant. I use Ollama for local model deployment on my M4 MacBook. What I noticed is that it struggles to handle concurrent requests efficiently. I gave vLLM a try, and the difference in high-throughput handling was noticeable. Long story short, vLLM is awesome for high-throughput serving -> wanted to understand exactly what sets it apart from Ollama -> read the original paper published by the vLLM team -> learned about continuous batching and PagedAttention -> spent hours building, debugging, and benchmarking my own implementation (with plenty of back-and-forth with an LLM, and even more back-and-forth with NaNs) -> and now I am blogging about it!

item.title: August 7: Facade Layer Design
item.author: asubedi@asubedi.com.np (Ashish Subedi)
item.description:
Hello everyone, welcome back! Today was a productive day for me as I got to work with pure SQL and fully implemented metering logic within a MySQL Stored Procedure. More about that coming soon!

For now, let’s talk about the facade design pattern. In my workplace, we have a facade layer implementation, which serves as a central point of communication for the frontend layer (and some backend APIs). The job of this layer is to provide endpoints of internal APIs to the public through the facade, hence the name. This is implemented in FastAPI.

item.title: About
item.author: asubedi@asubedi.com.np (Ashish Subedi)
item.description:
Greetings! I’m Ashish Subedi, a Backend & AI Systems Engineer with ~5 years of production experience across Python, Go, Document AI, OCR, RAG, and cloud infrastructure (AWS/GCP, Kubernetes). Right now I’m based in Saarbrücken, Germany, pursuing my M.Sc. in Computer Science (Informatik) at Saarland University, focusing on AI systems and security.

What I’ve Shipped

  • RTKData.com (Germany): Backend Software Engineer (Werkstudent) building high-throughput Go infrastructure for low-latency RTK/GNSS correction streams, automated rover failover, dynamic base-station switchover, and multi-rover SLO load testing.
  • Evana AG (Germany): AI & Backend Software Engineer (Werkstudent) who shipped Go and Python document pipelines, MistralOCR bounding-box layout retrieval, and hybrid-embedding RAG improvements.
  • Docsumo (Singapore, Remote): 3.5+ years as a Python Engineer shipping LLM/OCR extraction systems, fast ETL pipelines, and an architectural overhaul that cut document processing costs by 9x (the rare kind of refactor that makes both engineers and CFOs smile).
  • Earlier Stops: Migrated legacy services to AWS/EKS and built PostgreSQL usage-metering stored procedures at Belvy LLC, and worked on ML/CNN research at NAAMI.

Why This Site Exists

Long story short: I like taking things apart to see how they tick. Sometimes that means writing a miniature continuous-batching LLM engine from scratch just to understand why vLLM is fast; other times it means disassembling a 193 MB Go binary at 2 AM because my weekly AI quota vanished faster than free pizza at a department seminar.
